tasks.title: A custom Clone
tasks.statement: A struct Doc { title: String, version: u32 }. Implement Clone by hand so that the clone gets a version one higher and the same title.
tasks.hint: Clone the fields separately; add one to version.

tasks.title: Copy and Clone
tasks.statement: A struct Point { x: i32, y: i32 }: add a derive so that values are copied on assignment (Copy, Clone) and can be printed (Debug).
tasks.hint: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]

tasks.title: Default by hand
tasks.statement: A struct Settings { volume: u8, name: String, ratio: f64 }. Implement Default by hand: volume 50, name «по умолчанию», ratio 1.5.
tasks.hint: impl Default for Settings: the function default().

tasks.title: Equality of different types
tasks.statement: Structs Meters(f64) and Feet(f64). Implement PartialEq<Feet> for Meters: equal if the values match to within 0.001 (1 m = 3.28084 feet).
tasks.hint: Convert to feet and compare with a tolerance.

tasks.title: Task ordering
tasks.statement: A struct Task { pri: u32, name: String }. Implement Ord so that a larger priority counts as "greater", and on a tie the name that comes earlier alphabetically counts as "greater" (reversed name order). Add PartialOrd, Eq, PartialEq.
tasks.hint: then(other.name.cmp(&self.name)) reverses the name order.

tasks.title: Case-insensitive hash
tasks.statement: A struct CiKey(String): equal to another ignoring case. Implement PartialEq, Eq and Hash by hand, consistently (hash the lowercase string), so that a HashSet<CiKey> treats "Rust" and "rUST" as one key.
tasks.hint: Hash and equality use the same normalized key.

tasks.title: From for a struct
tasks.statement: A struct Rgb(u8, u8, u8). Implement From<(u8, u8, u8)>, From<[u8; 3]> and From<Rgb> for u32 (0xRRGGBB).
tasks.hint: Shifts << 16 and << 8.

tasks.title: TryFrom
tasks.statement: A struct Percent(u8). Implement TryFrom<i32> for Percent: Ok for 0..=100, otherwise Err(String) with the text «вне диапазона: <n>».
tasks.hint: (0..=100).contains(&n)

tasks.title: AsRef for a wrapper
tasks.statement: A struct Name(String). Implement AsRef<str> for Name and write a function shout(x: impl AsRef<str>) -> String (uppercase) that accepts &str, String and Name.
tasks.hint: &self.0: a String coerces to &str.

tasks.title: Deref for a wrapper
tasks.statement: A struct Stack(Vec<i32>). Implement Deref<Target = Vec<i32>> and DerefMut so that the vector methods len(), last(), push() work directly on Stack.
tasks.hint: Return a reference to the inner vector.

tasks.title: Index for a grid
tasks.statement: A struct Grid { w: usize, cells: Vec<char> }. Implement Index<(usize, usize)> and IndexMut<(usize, usize)>: g[(x, y)] is the cell in column x and row y.
tasks.hint: Index into the flat vector: y * w + x.

tasks.title: A custom Iterator: a Range with a step
tasks.statement: A struct Stepper { cur: i32, end: i32, step: i32 } (step > 0). Implement Iterator<Item = i32>: from cur up to end (exclusive) with step step.
tasks.hint: While cur < end, yield it and advance.

tasks.title: IntoIterator for your own collection
tasks.statement: A struct Bag { items: Vec<String> }. Implement IntoIterator for Bag (by value) and for &Bag (by reference), so that both for x in bag and for x in &bag work.
tasks.hint: Delegate to the vector: into_iter() and iter().

tasks.title: FromIterator
tasks.statement: A struct Bag { items: Vec<String> }. Implement FromIterator<&str> for Bag so that collect from an iterator of strings works: let b: Bag = words.into_iter().collect();
tasks.hint: Build a vector of String from an iterator of &str.

tasks.title: Extend and Sum
tasks.statement: A struct Money(i64). Implement std::iter::Sum for Money (the sum of Money values) and Extend<Money>... to keep it simple, only Sum and Add (Money + Money).
tasks.hint: fold(Money(0), |a, b| a + b)

tasks.title: Fn, FnMut, FnOnce
tasks.statement: Write three functions: call_twice(f: impl Fn() -> i32) -> i32 (the sum of two calls), call_mut(mut f: impl FnMut()) — call it 3 times, call_once(f: impl FnOnce() -> String) -> String — call it once.
tasks.hint: An FnOnce can be called only once: just f(), no repeats.

tasks.title: A list of closures
tasks.statement: Write compose_all(fs: Vec<Box<dyn Fn(i32) -> i32>>) -> Box<dyn Fn(i32) -> i32>: a function that applies all of them in order.
tasks.hint: Box::new(move |x| fs.iter().fold(x, |acc, f| f(acc)))

tasks.title: An error with a cause
tasks.statement: Declared: ConfigError { path: String, cause: std::num::ParseIntError }. Implement Display ("ошибка в <path>"), Error, and source() (returns Some(&self.cause)).
tasks.hint: source() returns Option<&dyn Error>.

tasks.title: Combining errors
tasks.statement: Declare an enum AppError { Parse(std::num::ParseIntError), Neg(i64) } with From<ParseIntError>, Display and Error. The function positive(s: &str) -> Result<i64, AppError> parses a number and returns Err(Neg(n)) for negative ones.
tasks.hint: ? turns ParseIntError into AppError via From.

tasks.title: Send and Sync
tasks.statement: Write the functions assert_send<T: Send>() and assert_sync<T: Sync>() (empty, a compile-time check). The driver main checks that String and Vec<i32> are Send, and Arc<Mutex<i32>> is Send and Sync. Your solution is just the function declarations.
tasks.hint: An empty body: the check happens when the type is substituted.

tasks.title: A dynamic type
tasks.statement: Write describe(v: &dyn std::any::Any) -> String: "целое N" for i32, "строка S" for String, "дробное X" for f64, otherwise "неизвестно" (downcast_ref).
tasks.hint: downcast_ref::<T>() returns Option<&T>.

tasks.title: Cow
tasks.statement: Write normalize(s: &str) -> std::borrow::Cow<str>: if the string contains tabs, return Owned with the tabs replaced by spaces, otherwise return Borrowed without copying. The driver checks the variant.
tasks.hint: Cow::Borrowed(s) copies nothing; Cow::Owned(String).

tasks.title: Typed identifiers
tasks.statement: A struct Id<T> { n: u32, _m: PhantomData<T> }. Implement new(n), get(&self), and Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Debug by hand without bounds on T (derive would require Clone for T). The types User and Order are empty structs. Comparing Id<User> with Id<Order> must not compile (there is nothing to test that with, just use PhantomData).
tasks.hint: PhantomData is a value with no data: Id { n, _m: PhantomData }.

tasks.title: Borrow and lookup
tasks.statement: Write find_len(m: &std::collections::HashMap<String, usize>, key: &str) -> usize: the value for the key or 0, looking up by &str in a map with String keys (the justification is the Borrow<str> trait).
tasks.hint: m.get(key) accepts &str because String: Borrow<str>.

tasks.title: Display and Debug together
tasks.statement: A struct Ver(u32, u32, u32). Implement Display as "1.2.3" and derive(Debug); the function show(v: &impl std::fmt::Display) -> String returns "версия <v>".
tasks.hint: Display gives you to_string() for free.

tasks.title: Trait bounds
tasks.statement: Write largest_by_key<T, K: Ord>(items: &[T], key: impl Fn(&T) -> K) -> Option<&T>: the element with the largest key (the first one on a tie).
tasks.hint: Replace best only when the key is strictly greater.

tasks.title: An associated type
tasks.statement: A trait Container { type Item; fn first(&self) -> Option<&Self::Item>; fn size(&self) -> usize; }. Implement it for the struct Words(Vec<String>) (Item = String).
tasks.hint: type Item = String; delegate the methods to the vector.

tasks.title: A supertrait
tasks.statement: A trait Named: fmt::Display + ... — declare trait Entity: std::fmt::Display { fn id(&self) -> u32; fn label(&self) -> String { format!("#{} {}", self.id(), self) } }. Implement Entity and Display for the struct Item { id: u32, name: String } (Display prints the name).
tasks.hint: The supertrait guarantees that Display is available inside the default method.

tasks.title: A blanket implementation
tasks.statement: A trait Shout { fn shout(&self) -> String; }. Implement it at once for every type that has Display (impl<T: Display> Shout for T): the text in uppercase with a "!".
tasks.hint: A blanket impl applies to any T: Display.

tasks.title: ?Sized
tasks.statement: Write byte_len<T: ?Sized + AsRef<[u8]>>(x: &T) -> usize: the length in bytes for str, slices and vectors (relaxing Sized lets you accept str and [u8] directly).
tasks.hint: x.as_ref().len(); T: ?Sized allows str and [u8].
